title: TV source certificates and level-set convergence

items.title: Distributional TV as an extended functional on L²
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be open and let $X=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. Every $u\in X$ is integrable on compact subsets by Cauchy–Schwarz. Define its extended distributional total variation by
$$TV_2(u;\Omega):=\sup\left\{\int_\Omega u\,\operatorname{div}\varphi\,dx:\ \varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^2),\ \sup_{x\in\Omega}|\varphi(x)|\le1\right\}\in[0,+\infty],$$
where $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^2)$ denotes smooth compactly supported vector fields, $|\cdot|$ is the Euclidean norm, and $\operatorname{div}\varphi=\partial_1\varphi_1+\partial_2\varphi_2$. This definition treats $L^2$ functions as almost-everywhere classes and does not require $u\in L^1(\Omega)$.

references.title: José A. Iglesias, Gwenael Mercier, and Otmar Scherzer, A note on convergence of solutions of total variation regularized linear inverse problems, §1.1
references.locator: §1.1, distributional TV for locally integrable functions

references.title: Gláucio Terra, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory — Lecture Notes, version 1.6, §7.4
references.locator: §7.4, distributional derivatives and local BV

items.title: Canonical TV level sets and their boundaries
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $u\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R)$, with functions identified when they agree almost everywhere. For full-space TV, use $u$ itself. For a bounded-domain Dirichlet or Neumann problem, use the zero extension $\widetilde u$ only to define the geometric level sets; this does not change the selected regularizer, and for each nonzero level the resulting set lies inside $\Omega$. For $t>0$, the positive $t$-level class is the measurable-set class of $E_t^+(u):=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:u(x)>t\}$; for $t<0$, the negative $t$-level class is the class of $E_t^-(u):=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:u(x)<t\}$. These classes do not depend on the representative of $u$. For any measurable set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, its density-one representative is

$$E^{(1)}:=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{|E\cap B(x,r)|}{|B(x,r)|}=1\right\}.$$

This representative depends only on the almost-everywhere class of $E$. The canonical level set $U_u^{(t)}$ is $(E_t^+(u))^{(1)}$ when $t>0$ and $(E_t^-(u))^{(1)}$ when $t<0$. Its canonical boundary is the ordinary topological boundary $\partial U_u^{(t)}$ in $\mathbb R^2$. For two nonempty boundary sets, use the usual extended Hausdorff distance induced by Euclidean distance; set $d_H(\varnothing,\varnothing)=0$ and $d_H(E,F)=+\infty$ if exactly one set is empty. Hausdorff convergence uses this convention and is invariant under changes to a function on a null set.

references.title: José A. Iglesias, Gwenael Mercier, and Otmar Scherzer, A note on convergence of solutions of total variation regularized linear inverse problems, §3
Antonin Chambolle, Vincent Duval, Gabriel Peyré, and Clarice Poon, Geometric properties of solutions to the total variation denoising problem, §2.1

items.title: Variational curvature of a finite-perimeter set
items.statement:
Let $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$ or let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain. Choose one of three perimeter functionals for measurable $E\subseteq\Omega$: full-space perimeter $P_R(E)=P(E;\mathbb R^2)$ when $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$; Neumann relative perimeter $P_N(E)=P(E;\Omega)$ on a bounded domain; or Dirichlet perimeter $P_D(E)=P(\widetilde E;\mathbb R^2)$, where $\widetilde E$ is $E$ extended by the empty set outside $\Omega$. Require finite measure and finite selected perimeter, and let $\kappa:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be Lebesgue-measurable with $\int_F|\kappa|<\infty$ for every set considered. The set $E$ has **variational curvature** $\kappa$ for the selected model if its selected perimeter minus $\int_E\kappa\,dx$ is no greater than the same quantity for every finite-measure finite-selected-perimeter competitor $F\subseteq\Omega$ whose symmetric difference $F\mathbin\triangle E$ has compact closure in $\Omega$. In the full-space model, this means compact closure in $\mathbb R^2$.

For bounded Dirichlet TV, a separate **obstacle curvature** condition on $\Omega$ means that $\Omega$, viewed as a finite-perimeter set in $\mathbb R^2$, minimizes $F\mapsto P(F;\mathbb R^2)-\int_F\kappa_\Omega\,dx$ over all finite-measure finite-perimeter $F\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ whose symmetric difference with $\Omega$ has compact closure in $\mathbb R^2$, where $\kappa_\Omega\in L^1(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R)$.

references.title: José A. Iglesias, Gwenael Mercier, and Otmar Scherzer, A note on convergence of solutions of total variation regularized linear inverse problems, Definition 4
Antonin Chambolle, Vincent Duval, Gabriel Peyré, and Clarice Poon, Geometric properties of solutions to the total variation denoising problem, §2.6

items.title: Finite L² distributional variation has a finite Radon derivative
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. If $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ is open, $u\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and $TV_2(u;\Omega)<\infty$, then each distributional derivative of $u$ is represented by a finite signed Radon measure. Their vector measure $Du$ has finite Radon variation and $|Du|(\Omega)=TV_2(u;\Omega)$.

references.title: José A. Iglesias, Gwenael Mercier, and Otmar Scherzer, A note on convergence of solutions of total variation regularized linear inverse problems, §1.1
references.locator: §1.1, representation of finite distributional variation as a Radon derivative

items.title: Convexity, lower semicontinuity, and BV agreement of L² TV
items.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be open and let $TV_2(\cdot;\Omega)$ be the extended distributional total variation on $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. It is proper, convex, lower semicontinuous in the $L^2$ norm, and positively one-homogeneous for nonnegative scalars. For every $u\in BV(\Omega)\cap L^2(\Omega)$, it agrees with spatial TV: $TV_2(u;\Omega)=TV(u;\Omega)$.

items.title: Dual source certificates for TV regularization
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$, or let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain. Set $X=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and let $Y=L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ for a measure space $(\Sigma,\mu)$, using the real integral inner products; under Countable Choice these are real Hilbert spaces. Let $A:X\to Y$ be bounded and real-linear, and let $A^*:Y\to X$ be its Hilbert adjoint, characterized by $\langle Au,p\rangle_Y=\langle u,A^*p\rangle_X$. Define $R:X\to[0,+\infty]$ as follows. If $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$, take $R(u)=TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)$, the supremum of $\int u\,\operatorname{div}\varphi$ over smooth compactly supported vector fields of Euclidean norm at most one. For bounded $\Omega$, either take Neumann TV, $R(u)=TV(u;\Omega)$ when $u\in BV(\Omega)$ and $+\infty$ otherwise, or Dirichlet TV, $R(u)=TV(\widetilde u;\mathbb R^2)$ when the zero extension $\widetilde u$ belongs to $BV(\mathbb R^2)$ and $+\infty$ otherwise. Thus the bounded-domain choices count, respectively, only the interior derivative or also the jump of the zero extension across the boundary. In the full-space case finite $R$ does not require global $L^1$ integrability.

Identify each $q\in X$ with the continuous linear functional $h\mapsto\langle q,h\rangle_X$ by the real Hilbert-space Riesz representation. For exact data $f=Au^\dagger$, a **minimum-TV exact solution** is a point $u^\dagger\in X$ satisfying $Au^\dagger=f$ and $R(u^\dagger)\le R(u)$ for every $u\in X$ with $Au=f$. A vector $p^\dagger\in Y$ is a **dual source certificate** for $u^\dagger$ if $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$, where $\partial R$ is the convex subdifferential on the real Banach space $X$. The **TV source condition** at $u^\dagger$ is that such a certificate exists; it does not assert uniqueness of the truth or of the certificate. For a chosen certificate, the associated Bregman distance is

$$D_R^{A^*p^\dagger}(u,u^\dagger):=R(u)-R(u^\dagger)-\langle A^*p^\dagger,u-u^\dagger\rangle_X,$$

for $u\in\operatorname{dom}R$.

references.title: José A. Iglesias, Gwenael Mercier, and Otmar Scherzer, A note on convergence of solutions of total variation regularized linear inverse problems, Definition 1
Antonin Chambolle, Vincent Duval, Gabriel Peyré, and Clarice Poon, Geometric properties of solutions to the total variation denoising problem, §§1.3 and 3.1
Barbara Kaltenbacher, Convergence rates under a range invariance condition with application to electrical impedance tomography, Definition (1.25)

items.title: Sharp planar isoperimetric inequality for finite-perimeter sets
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Every Lebesgue-measurable set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ with finite area and finite perimeter satisfies
$$4\pi |E|\le P(E;\mathbb R^2)^2.$$

references.locator: §3.4, planar isoperimetric estimate used in the density argument

items.title: Compactly supported BV cutoffs for finite-variation L² functions
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. If $u\in L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R)$ and $TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)<\infty$, there exist smooth cutoffs $\chi_k$ with $0\le\chi_k\le1$, $\chi_k=1$ on $B(0,k)$, support in $B(0,2k)$, and $\sup_{k\ge1}k\|\nabla\chi_k\|_\infty<\infty$. For every family satisfying these four conditions, $v_k:=\chi_ku$ belongs to $BV(\mathbb R^2)\cap L^1(\mathbb R^2)$, has support in $B(0,2k)$, converges to $u$ in $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$, and
$$\limsup_{k\to\infty}TV(v_k;\mathbb R^2)\le TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2).$$

references.title: José A. Iglesias, Gwenael Mercier, and Otmar Scherzer, A note on convergence of solutions of total variation regularized linear inverse problems, §1.1
references.locator: §1.1, full-plane L² TV and cutoff approximation

items.title: Dual attainment and convergence of TV source certificates
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and $Y=L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $A:X\to Y$ be bounded and real-linear, and let $R:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be one of the full-space, Dirichlet, or Neumann TV functionals. Assume that $R$ is proper, convex, lower semicontinuous, and positively one-homogeneous, and that $u^\dagger$ is a minimum-$R$ exact solution of $Au=f$ with a dual source certificate $p^\dagger\in Y$, so $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$. Define $K:=\{p\in Y:A^*p\in\partial R(0)\}$ and $D_{\alpha,w}(p):=\langle f+w,p\rangle_Y-\frac{\alpha}{2}\|p\|_Y^2$ for $\alpha>0$ and $w\in Y$.

For each $\alpha>0$ and $w\in Y$, $D_{\alpha,w}$ has a unique maximizer $p_{\alpha,w}=\operatorname{Proj}_K((f+w)/\alpha)$. If $u_{\alpha,w}$ is any supplied global minimizer of $u\mapsto\frac12\|Au-(f+w)\|_Y^2+\alpha R(u)$, then $p_{\alpha,w}=(f+w-Au_{\alpha,w})/\alpha$, $A^*p_{\alpha,w}\in\partial R(u_{\alpha,w})$, and $A^*p_{\alpha,w}\in\partial R(0)$. For every such supplied minimizer, the correctly normalized primal-dual value identity is

$$\min_u\{\tfrac12\|Au-(f+w)\|_Y^2+\alpha R(u)\}=\alpha D_{\alpha,w}(p_{\alpha,w}).$$

Let $P_0:=\{p\in K:\langle f,p\rangle_Y=R(u^\dagger)\}$ and let $p_0$ be its unique minimum-norm element. For every sequence $\alpha_n>0$ with $\alpha_n\to0$, $p_{\alpha_n,0}\to p_0$ strongly in $Y$ and $A^*p_{\alpha_n,0}\to A^*p_0$ strongly in $X$. For every $\alpha>0$ and $w\in Y$,

$$\|p_{\alpha,w}-p_{\alpha,0}\|_Y\le\frac{\|w\|_Y}{\alpha},\qquad \|A^*p_{\alpha,w}-A^*p_{\alpha,0}\|_X\le\frac{\|A^*\|\,\|w\|_Y}{\alpha}.$$

Moreover, for any $R_0>R(u^\dagger)$ the certificate yields a variational source condition on $\{u:R(u)\le R_0\}$ with exponent $2$, coefficient $\beta=0$, and index function $\psi(s)=(1+\|p^\dagger\|_Y)\sqrt{s}$. Consequently, if $\delta_n\downarrow0$, $\|w_n\|_Y\le\delta_n$, $\alpha_n\asymp\delta_n$, and exact global minimizers $u_n$ are supplied, then the variational-source rate theorem gives

$$D_R^{A^*p^\dagger}(u_n,u^\dagger)=O(\delta_n),\qquad \|Au_n-(f+w_n)\|_Y=O(\delta_n).$$

references.title: José A. Iglesias, Gwenael Mercier, and Otmar Scherzer, A note on convergence of solutions of total variation regularized linear inverse problems, Theorem 1, Proposition 3, and their complete proofs
Barbara Kaltenbacher, Convergence rates under a range invariance condition with application to electrical impedance tomography, Lemma 2 and Theorem 3
Jonathan M. Borwein and Jon D. Vanderwerff, Convex Functions: Constructions, Characterizations and Counterexamples, Exercise 4.4.1

items.title: Coarea for finite-variation L² functions
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $u\in L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)<\infty$. For $t>0$ set $E_t^+=\{x:u(x)>t\}$, and for $t<0$ set $E_t^-=\{x:u(x)<t\}$. Each set has finite area, almost every applicable level set has finite perimeter, and
$$TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)=\int_0^\infty P(E_t^+;\mathbb R^2)\,dt+\int_{-\infty}^0P(E_t^-;\mathbb R^2)\,dt.$$

references.title: José A. Iglesias, Gwenael Mercier, and Otmar Scherzer, A note on convergence of solutions of total variation regularized linear inverse problems, §3.1
references.locator: §3.1, coarea and finite-perimeter level sets for L² solutions

items.title: Full-space BV Sobolev inequality for L² distributional TV
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Every $u\in L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R)$ with $TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)<\infty$ satisfies
$$\|u\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^2)}\le TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2).$$

items.title: BV Sobolev–Poincaré inequality for Neumann TV
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For every nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, there is a finite constant $C_\Omega>0$ such that every $u\in BV(\Omega)$ satisfies
$$\|u-u_\Omega\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega TV(u;\Omega),\qquad u_\Omega:=|\Omega|^{-1}\int_\Omega u\,dx.$$

items.title: Primal compactness and selection of a minimum-TV limit
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and let $Y=L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ be real Hilbert spaces. Let $A:X\to Y$ be bounded and real-linear, let $f=Au^\dagger$, and assume $u^\dagger$ is an exact solution minimizing a proper, convex, lower semicontinuous, positively one-homogeneous TV functional $R:X\to[0,+\infty]$ with a source certificate $p^\dagger\in Y$, so $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$. Use full-space $R=TV_2(\cdot;\mathbb R^2)$ if $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$; for a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, use either Neumann $R(u)=TV(u;\Omega)$ or Dirichlet $R(u)=TV(\widetilde u;\mathbb R^2)$ for the zero extension $\widetilde u$, assigning $+\infty$ outside the respective finite-variation domain. A bounded connected Lipschitz domain here is a nonempty bounded open set with a finite Lipschitz graph cover of its boundary, with the domain on one side of each graph, and with no separation into two disjoint nonempty relatively open sets.

Let $\alpha_n>0$ tend to zero, let $w_n\in Y$, and suppose $\|A^*\|\,\|w_n\|_Y/\alpha_n\le\eta$ for some finite $\eta$. For each $n$, suppose a supplied global minimizer $u_n\in X$ minimizes
$$J_n(u)=\tfrac12\|Au-(f+w_n)\|_Y^2+\alpha_nR(u).$$
In the Neumann case, if $A\mathbf1_\Omega=0$, take $u_n$ after subtracting its mean $|\Omega|^{-1}\int_\Omega u_n$; this leaves $J_n$ unchanged. Then a subsequence converges weakly in $L^2(\Omega)$ and, in addition, strongly in $L^1(\Omega)$ when $\Omega$ is bounded or strongly in $L^1$ on every bounded ball when $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$. Its limit $u_0$ is an exact solution $Au_0=f$ minimizing $R$ among exact solutions, and $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u_0)$.

references.title: José A. Iglesias, Gwenael Mercier, and Otmar Scherzer, A note on convergence of solutions of total variation regularized linear inverse problems, Lemma 1 and proof
references.locator: Lemma 1, proof on full-space and bounded-domain BV compactness

references.title: Gláucio Terra, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory — Lecture Notes, version 1.6
references.locator: Theorem 7.49 and proof; §§7.4–7.5 on extension and compactness

items.title: Uniform density and Hausdorff convergence of TV level-set boundaries
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)\to L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ be bounded and real-linear, let $f=Au^\dagger$, and suppose $u^\dagger$ is a minimum-TV exact solution with a source certificate $p^\dagger$. For $\alpha_n>0$ tending to zero and noises $w_n\in L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$, assume $\|A^*\|\|w_n\|_2/\alpha_n\le\eta$ and let $u_n$ be supplied global minimizers of $\frac12\|Au-(f+w_n)\|_2^2+\alpha_n TV(u)$. Define $p_n=(f+w_n-Au_n)/\alpha_n$ and $v_n=A^*p_n$. Use $TV_2$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ for full-space TV; on a nonempty bounded Lipschitz domain use zero-extension Dirichlet TV, and on a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz domain use relative Neumann TV. For bounded-domain geometry use the ambient zero-extended level sets and their topological boundaries in $\mathbb R^2$.

For full-space or Dirichlet TV, assume $\eta<2\sqrt\pi$; in the bounded Dirichlet case also assume $\Omega$ has global obstacle curvature $\kappa_\Omega\in L^1(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R)$ with $\kappa_\Omega\ge g$ almost everywhere outside $\Omega$ for some real-valued $g\in L^2(\mathbb R^2\setminus\Omega;\mathbb R)$. For Neumann TV, let $C_\Omega$ be a constant from the BV Sobolev–Poincaré inequality $\|u-u_\Omega\|_2\le C_\Omega TV(u;\Omega)$ and assume $\eta<1/C_\Omega$.

For almost every nonzero $t$, the level set $E_n(t)$ has finite measure and perimeter, minimizes the branch-specific perimeter minus $\int_{E}\operatorname{sgn}(t)v_n$ under compactly supported perturbations, and satisfies $P(E_n(t))=\operatorname{sgn}(t)\int_{E_n(t)}v_n$. There are constants $c>0$ and $r_0>0$, independent of $n$ and almost every such $t$, such that for every $x\in\partial E_n(t)$ and $0<r<r_0$,
$$|B(x,r)\cap E_n(t)|\ge c|B(x,r)|,\qquad |B(x,r)\setminus E_n(t)|\ge c|B(x,r)|.$$
In the full-space branch all these level sets are contained in one common ball; in the bounded branches they lie in $\overline\Omega$. The same density and support conclusions are asserted for any selected minimum-TV exact limit that carries the inherited source certificate, using zero noise. Whenever the corresponding level sets converge in measure, their canonical boundaries converge in Hausdorff distance.

references.title: José A. Iglesias, Gwenael Mercier, and Otmar Scherzer, A note on convergence of solutions of total variation regularized linear inverse problems, Lemmas 3–7 and §§3.4, 4.1–4.3

items.title: Two-dimensional TV level-set convergence under a source condition
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)\to L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ be bounded and real-linear, let $f=Au^\dagger$, and suppose $u^\dagger$ is a minimum-TV exact solution with a dual source certificate $p^\dagger$, meaning $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$. Use $R=TV_2$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ for full-space TV; for a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz domain use either Dirichlet TV of the zero extension or Neumann TV relative to $\Omega$. Let $\alpha_n>0$ tend to zero, let $w_n\in L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $\|A^*\|\|w_n\|_2/\alpha_n\le\eta$, and suppose a global minimizer $u_n$ is supplied for each functional
$$u\longmapsto\tfrac12\|Au-(f+w_n)\|_2^2+\alpha_nR(u).$$
For full-space or Dirichlet TV, assume $\eta<2\sqrt\pi$; for bounded Dirichlet TV also assume $\Omega$ has global obstacle curvature $\kappa_\Omega\in L^1(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R)$ with $\kappa_\Omega\ge g$ almost everywhere outside $\Omega$ for some real-valued $g\in L^2(\mathbb R^2\setminus\Omega;\mathbb R)$. For Neumann TV, let $C_\Omega$ be a constant satisfying $\|u-u_\Omega\|_2\le C_\Omega TV(u;\Omega)$ on $BV(\Omega)$ and assume $\eta<1/C_\Omega$. In the Neumann case with $A\mathbf1_\Omega=0$, choose the minimizers after subtracting their means.

There is a subsequence $(u_{n_k})$ and a selected minimum-TV exact solution $u_0$ such that $Au_0=f$ and, for almost every nonzero $t$, the canonical level sets of $u_{n_k}$ converge in measure to the canonical level set of $u_0$, while their canonical ambient boundaries converge in Hausdorff distance. The limit $u_0$ need not equal the initially named truth $u^\dagger$ unless the minimum-TV exact solution is unique.

title: TV source certificates and level-set convergence — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A minimum-TV truth can lack an L² source certificate
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. The claim that every minimum-TV exact truth in a two-dimensional Neumann model has an $L^2$ source certificate is false. Let $\Omega=(-1,1)^2$, let $X=Y=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, let $A:X\to Y$ be the identity, let $f=u^\dagger$ with $u^\dagger(x_1,x_2)=|x_1|$, and let the regularizer be the Neumann total variation $R(u)=|Du|(\Omega)$ on $BV(\Omega)\cap L^2(\Omega)$ and $R(u)=+\infty$ otherwise. The exact equation $Au=f$ has the unique solution $u^\dagger$, so it is a minimum-TV exact truth. Nevertheless, there is no $p\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ such that $A^*p=p\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$, where $p\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$ means $R(v)\ge R(u^\dagger)+\int_\Omega p(v-u^\dagger)\,dx$ for every $v\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$.

references.title: Antonin Chambolle, Vincent Duval, Gabriel Peyré, and Clarice Poon, Geometric properties of solutions to the total variation denoising problem, §§1.3 and 7
references.locator: §7, limitations of L² source certificates for nonsmooth TV solutions

items.title: Circular Radon inversion at the zero truth
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\sigma$ be the surface measure on $S^1$ used in the polar-coordinate formula, let $\Sigma=S^1\times(0,2)$ with product measure $\sigma\times dt$, and for real Schwartz functions $u\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R)$ define
$$(A_0u)(z,t)=t\int_{S^1}u(z+t\omega)\,d\sigma(\omega),\qquad z\in S^1,\quad 0<t<2.$$
The map $A_0$ has a unique bounded extension $A:L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R)\to L^2(\Sigma;\mathbb R)$. For full-space $TV_2$, exact datum $f=0$, zero truth $u^\dagger=0$, and certificate $p^\dagger=0$, the truth is a minimum-TV exact solution satisfying the source condition. For every sequence $\alpha_n>0$ tending to zero, $w_n=0$, and $u_n=0$, each $u_n$ is a global minimizer of the quadratic TV functional and all nonzero canonical level sets and boundaries of $u_n$ and $u^\dagger$ are empty; their measure and extended Hausdorff distances are zero.

references.title: José A. Iglesias, Gwenael Mercier, and Otmar Scherzer, A note on convergence of solutions of total variation regularized linear inverse problems, §5.1
references.locator: §5.1, definition (41) and boundedness of the circular Radon transform

items.title: A smooth Bessel-blur truth with an explicit TV source certificate
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $0<a<b$, let $\phi\in C_c^\infty((a,b))$ be nonnegative and not identically zero, define $U(r)=\int_r^b\phi(s)\,ds$ for $r\ge0$, and set $u^\dagger(x)=U(|x|)$ on $\mathbb R^2$. Choose $h\in C_c^\infty((a/2,2b))$ with $0\le h\le1$ and $h=1$ on $\operatorname{supp}\phi$, put $z(x)=h(|x|)x/|x|$ extended by zero at the origin, and let $q=\operatorname{div}z$. On real $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ define the Bessel blur $A=\mathcal F_2^{-1}M_m\mathcal F_2$, where $\mathcal F_2$ is the unitary Fourier transform with phase $e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}$ and $M_m$ multiplies by $m(\xi)=(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{-1/2}$. Let $f=Au^\dagger$ and define $p=\mathcal F_2^{-1}\bigl((1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{1/2}\widehat q(\xi)\bigr)$. Then $A$ is bounded, self-adjoint, and injective, $p\in L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R)$, and $A^*p\in\partial TV_2(u^\dagger)$. Thus $u^\dagger$ is the unique minimum-TV exact solution satisfying the full-space source condition; for zero noise the parameter ratio $\|A^*\|\|w_n\|_2/\alpha_n$ is zero.

references.title: José A. Iglesias, Gwenael Mercier, and Otmar Scherzer, A note on convergence of solutions of total variation regularized linear inverse problems, §§5.1–5.2
references.locator: §5.1, smooth mollified truth source condition; §5.2, deblurring context
